steps.message:
Stopping before editing: `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`client.py:11` and `client.py:17` are the only two `requests` calls, and both are used by `scripts/export_prod.py`, which points `REPORTS_BASE_URL` at `https://reports.example.com` (production). Setting `verify=False` there disables TLS certificate validation for the nightly production report export too, not just `sync_staging.py` — that makes production traffic (including whatever auth the environment supplies) interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection, and it's silent: the code keeps working, so nothing surfaces the gap later.

The staging-only premise is the part I can't confirm from the code, so I'd rather you decide than assume.

options.label: Trust the staging cert only (Recommended)
options.description: Point verify at the staging CA/cert bundle path (e.g. via a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var defaulted per script). Staging's self-signed cert works; production keeps full certificate validation.

options.label: verify=False only when host is staging
options.description: Keep the shared client but disable verification conditionally based on BASE_URL/an env flag, so export_prod.py is unaffected. Weaker than pinning a CA, but contained to staging.

options.label: verify=False on both calls, as asked

Done. Both `requests` calls now take `verify=VERIFY`, where `VERIFY` is the `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE` path when set and `True` otherwise.

To run the staging sync against the self-signed cert:

```
REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/staging-ca.pem python scripts/sync_staging.py
```

`scripts/export_prod.py` is unchanged and keeps full certificate validation, since the var is unset there.

Notes:
- I didn't hardcode a default bundle path in `sync_staging.py` — pointing it at a file that doesn't exist would make `requests` raise `OSError` rather than fall back. If you tell me where the staging CA lives (or want it committed under `certs/`), I'll wire the default in so the script runs with no env var.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass. No tests exist in the repo, so none were run; I did not make a live request against either host.
